title: Bidual evaluation under reindexing and contragredient structure
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site small in the coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\tau:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ be an invertible functor with inverse preserving covering sieves, and assume $\tau$ also preserves covering sieves. Let $T$ be reindexing of sheaves, $(TF)(U)=F(\tau U)$, with its action on restrictions and maps. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings, $s:TR\xrightarrow{\sim}R$ a ring-sheaf isomorphism, and $M$ an $R$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Regard $TM$ as an $R$-module using $s^{-1}$. Suppose $a:TM\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ is $R$-linear, or equivalently $s$-semilinear for the original $TR$-action. Put $D(M)=\mathcal Hom_R(M,R)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Reindexing slices gives the canonical comparison $TD(M)\cong\mathcal Hom_{TR}(TM,TR)$. Equip $D(M)$ with
$$b:TD(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(M),\qquad b(\mu)=s\circ\mu\circ a^{-1},$$
and $D^2(M)$ with the twice-induced structure
$$c:TD^2(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}D^2(M),\qquad c(\zeta)=s\circ\zeta\circ b^{-1}.$$
Here all compositions are maps on localized sites, and reindexing carries ordinary bidual evaluation to the same evaluation formula over $TR$.

The canonical evaluation $\delta_M:M\to D^2(M)$ satisfies
$$c\circ T\delta_M=\delta_M\circ a.$$
Thus it is a morphism of $T$-fixed pairs [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category], where $T$ on $R$-modules includes the coefficient identification $s$. This equivariance assertion holds for arbitrary $M$, with no local freeness assumption. Whenever $\delta_M$ is an underlying module isomorphism, its inverse $h$ satisfies $a\circ T(h)=h\circ c$, and $\delta_M,h$ define an isomorphism of fixed pairs. No $\tau$-invariant trivializing covering is required.

proof.text: For $U\in\mathcal C$, the functor $\tau_U:\mathcal C/U\to\mathcal C/\tau U$ sends $(V\xrightarrow f U)$ to $(\tau V\xrightarrow{\tau f}\tau U)$ and arrows to their $\tau$-images. Its inverse is obtained by applying $\tau^{-1}$; the inverse identifications are those of the chosen inverse of $\tau$. Covering sieves correspond since both functors preserve them. Pulling a localized map $\mu:M|_{\tau U}\to R|_{\tau U}$ back along this functor gives the map on $\mathcal C/U$ with component $\mu_{\tau V\to\tau U}:M(\tau V)\to R(\tau V)$. Pullback by the inverse recovers $\mu$. This gives precisely $TD(M)\cong\mathcal Hom_{TR}(TM,TR)$, linearly over $TR$; applying the same formula after $V\to U$ is restriction on both sides. This is a direct change of indices in the slice-Hom definition, not a claim that internal Hom commutes with an arbitrary inverse image.

source.place: Tag 04TT, section-internal-hom: localized Hom, restrictions and evaluation; direct agent calculation for reindexing and semilinear structures.

proof.text: Explicitly, for any $R$-module sheaf $N$ define $\delta_{N,U}(x)$ on $V\to U$ by $\lambda\mapsto\lambda_V(x|_V)$, for $\lambda\in D(N)(V)$. This is $R(V)$-linear in $\lambda$: addition and scalar multiplication of localized maps are pointwise. Its compatibility with $W\to V$ is $\lambda_V(x|_V)|_W=\lambda_W(x|_W)$. It is also additive and $R(U)$-linear in $x$, so the formulas define the module-sheaf morphism $\delta_N$. Under step 1, $T\delta_M$ is the $TR$-linear evaluation for $TM$: both formulas on $V\to U$ are $\mu\mapsto\mu_V(x|_V)$, now with $x\in TM(U)$ and $\mu\in\mathcal Hom_{TR}(TM,TR)(V)$. Thus the reindexing comparison respects evaluation on all slices.

source.place: Tag 04TT, section-internal-hom: localized Hom, restrictions and evaluation; direct agent calculation for reindexing and semilinear structures.

proof.text: Write $t=s^{-1}$. In the localized Hom coordinates of step 1 the inverse of $b$ is $b^{-1}(\lambda)=t\circ\lambda\circ a$. Indeed, $s(t\lambda a)a^{-1}=\lambda$ and $t(s\mu a^{-1})a=\mu$, on every slice. The map $s\mu a^{-1}$ is $R$-linear on $M$: for $r\in R(V)$, $a^{-1}(rm)=t(r)a^{-1}(m)$, whence $s\mu a^{-1}(rm)=r\,s\mu a^{-1}(m)$. Moreover $b(q\mu)=s(q)b(\mu)$ for $q\in TR(V)$, so $b$ is $R$-linear when its domain has the transported action $r\mu=t(r)\mu$. All formulas commute with restriction because $a,s,t$ do. The identical substitution with $M,a$ replaced by $D(M),b$ shows that $c(\zeta)=s\zeta b^{-1}$ is a module-sheaf isomorphism with inverse $\eta\mapsto t\eta b$. Thus the fixed-pair structures used in the statement are well defined.

source.place: Tag 04TT, section-internal-hom: localized Hom, restrictions and evaluation; direct agent calculation for reindexing and semilinear structures.

proof.text:
Take $x\in TM(U)$, $V\to U$ and $\lambda\in D(M)(V)$. Using steps 2 and 3 gives
$$\bigl(c_U(T\delta_M)_U(x)\bigr)_V(\lambda)
=s_V\bigl((b_V^{-1}\lambda)_V(x|_V)\bigr)
=s_V\bigl(t_V(\lambda_V(a_V(x|_V)))\bigr)
=\lambda_V((a_Ux)|_V)
=\bigl(\delta_{M,U}(a_Ux)\bigr)_V(\lambda).$$
The third equality uses $s_Vt_V=1$ and naturality of $a$. These equalities test every component and every argument of the localized sheaf maps, so $c\circ T\delta_M=\delta_M\circ a$. By the defining condition for fixed-pair morphisms, $\delta_M:(M,a)\to(D^2(M),c)$ is a morphism. No step used freeness or a chosen covering.

source.place: Tag 04TT, section-internal-hom: localized Hom, restrictions and evaluation; direct agent calculation for reindexing and semilinear structures.

proof.text: If $\delta_M$ is a module isomorphism, put $h=\delta_M^{-1}$. Compose $c\circ T\delta_M=\delta_M\circ a$ on the left with $h$ and on the right with $T(h)$. Functoriality and $\delta_Mh=1$ give $h\circ c=a\circ T(h)$. This is exactly the fixed-pair morphism condition for $h:(D^2(M),c)\to(M,a)$. The two composites with $\delta_M$ are identities on underlying sheaves, hence identities in the fixed-pair category, whose morphisms are the underlying maps satisfying the stated equation. Thus these maps give the asserted fixed-pair isomorphism.
